newsitem.title: CANADA: Seagram says TV liqor ad ban no longer valid.
newsitem.headline: Seagram says TV liqor ad ban no longer valid.

text.p: The voluntary ban on liqor advertisements on televison and radio in the United States is no longer valid Seagram Co said on Wednesday.

"We believe strongly that the voluntary advertising ban that marketers of distilled spirits imposed first on radio and then on television in the thirties and forties is no longer appropriate," Seagram president and chief executive Edgar Bronfman Jr told the company's annual meeting.
After the meeting, Bronfman told reporters that Seagram plans to continue with its television ads for whiskey in certain U.S. markets despite a backlash against the ads.
"We have limited advertising in some U.S. markets and we're going to continue to advertize responsibly and carefully," he said.

Bronfman said the ads will continue despite concerns expressed by certain Congressional representatives and the chairman of the Federal Communication Commission that they may have an impact on children.
"They don't change our thinking," Bronfman said.
In his speech, Bronfman said there is no rational basis for excluding electronic media ads for distilled spirits beverages while allowing ads for wine and beer.
"In fact, federal regulators' attempts to generate a controversy based on a false distinction run counter to all of the educational efforts of scores of federal and state agencies," Bronfman said.

At the annual meeting, Bronfman said he expected the company's revenues in its Seagram Beverage Group, which declined 8 percent in the first quarter, to increase in the next quarter and for the rest of the fiscal year ending June 30.
Bronfman said he expected favourable earnings comparisons at 80 percent-owned MCA Inc as the year progressed.
"We still expect MCA to improve in the time frame that we initially cited. The progress is clear. The progress is strong. We are pleased with both the management and the business," he said.
Bronfman declined to comment on a court dispute between Seagram and Viacom Inc over joint ownership of television cable channel operator USA Networks.

"I do believe that the resolution of disputes should occur between the parties and not in court. That's the best way to resolve differences. Unfortunately, we've been unable to do so," he said after the meeting.
Stockholders at the annual meeting defeated a minority shareholder's motion to split Seagram into a beverages company and entertainment concern.
Seagram chairman Edgar Bronfman said the company would be glad to acquire the 20 percent of MCA Inc it did not own, but was satisfied with Matsushita Electric Industrial Co as a minority partner.
